commit.subject: LU-20290 lnet: add servicenode discovery visibility policy
commit.message:
LU-20290 lnet: add servicenode discovery visibility policy

Add a discovery visibility policy that partitions local server NIDs by
servicenode.

Servicenode membership is provided explicitly through a new internal
LNet API rather than inferred from interface topology.

LNetDiscServiceNodePolicySet() alone controls whether the runtime policy is
active. Activation must not depend on registered servicenodes because
discovery starts before Lustre targets register. Otherwise the node could
advertise all NIDs during startup and cause peers to merge them permanently
into one multi-rail peer.

Allow an administrator to declare servicenode visibility as required from
LNet initialization with external_disc_visibility=servicenode. Required and
ready state are separate: until Lustre enables the policy and publishes a
usable view generation, discovery GET and Push advertisement fail closed.
Readiness is cleared before a required provider is disabled and published only
after a successful enable; successful transitions and usable rollback state
then force Push updates to peers.

Membership can change while LNet is running. Policy changes are published
atomically, while membership changes rebuild the discovery views without
changing the active policy set.

Publish the active-policy count with release ordering and acquire it once in
lockless full-view readers. Policy objects are static, so retired array slots
are left intact rather than cleared; a reader that observed the old count can
therefore finish without dereferencing a cleared slot.

The policy does not permit the unrestricted merged view on non-loopback
networks. Local NIs not covered by a servicenode are exposed as singleton
partitions. Overlapping servicenode groups are folded because a shared NID
inevitably causes peers to merge them.

Servicenode and self/NUMA grouping are alternative peer-partitioning policies.
While enabled, servicenode is authoritative and supersedes the
topology-derived group policy, preventing a servicenode from being split into
multiple discovery peers. The configured group policy becomes active again
when servicenode is disabled.

This patch introduces the LNet servicenode visibility policy and its internal
interfaces. Subsequent patches populate servicenode membership from Lustre.
